events.label: ADP private payrolls (7:15 AM ET) — consensus 48K vs 44K prior; Fed Beige Book and EIA inventories same day
events.note: A soft private-payrolls print with September hike odds above 60% is the stagflation combination in its clearest form. Directional only; Friday's BLS print is the gate.

events.label: ISM Services (10:00 AM ET) — consensus 53.7 vs 53.6 prior; the prices component is the tell
events.note: Services is two-thirds of the economy and where a $94 barrel reaches consumer prices first. A services prices component above 70 makes the manufacturing Prices Index at 71.1 a trend rather than a sector quirk.

events.label: August jobs report (BLS, 8:30 AM ET) — first post-Warsh payrolls print; September FOMC gate
events.note: Last major labour print before the Sep 15-16 FOMC. Above 200K with average hourly earnings over 0.3% takes hike odds past 70% and pressures a 30Y close above 5.30%; under 150K sets the revised-down openings data against an ISM Prices Index stuck at 71.1.

events.label: AVGO Q3 FY2026 earnings (est.) — through $380 structural support; VMware + AI concentration dual overhang
events.note: Updated Aug 19 night: AVGO fell 5% to ~$362 on August 19, breaking through $380 structural support. VMware CVE-2026-59310 active exploitation (361 IPs, 47 countries per Aug 14 disclosure) + 72% AI revenue concentration (~72% of next-quarter sequential growth) create dual overhang. At ~65x trailing P/E, any miss or margin compression compounds. Q3 FY2026 results (est. September 4–5) are the first public accounting of both: VMware remediation costs in financial guidance, enterprise customer commentary on the incident, and AI revenue breadth. $380 is now resistance; $340–350 is the next structured support zone. Flip: recovery above $380 on volume, or formal VMware incident-containment statement before earnings.

events.label: Labor Day — US equity and bond markets closed
events.note: Cash markets shut for the session. Crypto and oil trade the weekend's Strait of Hormuz headlines unhedged, so a transit-suspension escalation over the long weekend gaps into Tuesday's open — eight days before the FOMC.

events.label: Canada retaliatory tariffs effective — dairy, appliances, ag equipment, pulp, paper, electronics
events.note: Updated Aug 28 night: Warsh's full Jackson Hole speech was hawkish — September hike odds rose to 59% from 33%. Warsh did not explicitly cite Canada tariff cost-push in the speech, leaving the tariff-inflation linkage as an open variable in the September 8-16 window. Tariffs arrive 4 days after the August jobs report (Sept 4) and 8 days before September 16 FOMC. With hike odds already at 59%, if hot jobs data and tariff cost-push both enter Fed communications between September 8 and 16, September hike odds above 65% are the two-variable scenario. DXY rose 0.4% to 99.50 on the Warsh hawkish signal — any tariff escalation that re-prices the dollar is the third input.

events.label: Oracle Q1 FY2027 results — first large AI-capex print since the Anthropic-Lambda deal
events.note: Carries a planned $20B equity issuance to fund AI infrastructure alongside the print. Read-through to how the market is pricing debt- and equity-funded datacenter buildout after Nvidia turned lessor on the $35B Lambda-Anthropic contract.

events.label: Bessent Treasury long-dated buyback ops begin — $4B+ per op, 10-20yr and 20-30yr bonds
events.note: Added Aug 19 night: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced August 19 the department will double the size of long-dated bond buyback operations, raising the maximum per-operation from $2B to at least $4B for bonds maturing in the 10-to-20-year and 20-to-30-year ranges. Effective September 9, runs through November 4 (end of current refunding quarter). The program provides structural demand support for the long end. If underlying supply dynamics overwhelm the $4B+ buyback, the 30Y could reassert above 5.25% before or during the program. BTC's structural debasement bid is partially underwritten by the buyback program as a signal of Treasury demand-management.

events.label: FOMC decision (Sep 15-16) — September rate path; market prices 68% odds of a hike
events.note: Updated Aug 31 morning: Four inputs now determine the vote. August jobs (Sept 4), Canada tariffs (Sept 8), Warsh communications Sept 8-16, and the Iran oil channel — US-Iran exchange on Aug 31 pushed Brent above $90; if sustained, it adds 20-30bps to headline CPI and enters Fed communications. September hike odds 57% on CME FedWatch (from 59% at Aug 28 close). 30Y at 5.21% on Aug 31, 9bps inside the 5.30% regime trigger; touched 5.31% intraday last week without a close confirmation. The Bessent buyback program starts September 9 with structural demand suppressing equilibrium 30Y yields by an estimated 10-15bps.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
